prompt.brief: Design an omnichannel contact center with voice and text virtual agents, live transcription, intent/routing, sentiment and quality analytics, and safe escalation to human agents.
successSignals: Define conversation/session state, audio and text events, transcript confidence, intent, sentiment, routing, consent, recording, and retention.
Keep turn latency predictable with streaming ASR/NLU/TTS, bounded context, interruption handling, handoff, and idempotent external actions.
Separate real-time media from asynchronous transcription, QA analytics, knowledge retrieval, workforce routing, and model training.
Explain PII/PCI redaction, safety escalation, provider outage, auditability, observability, and a human-first degraded mode.

functional: Start voice/chat sessions, authenticate customers, stream turns, transcribe, detect intent, retrieve approved answers, and synthesize responses.
Route to queues or agents, transfer context, record consented transcripts, analyze sentiment/quality, and expose supervisor dashboards.
Support recording deletion, redaction, callback/retry safety, provider failover, human escalation, model/version rollback, and audit export.
nonFunctional: Return conversational turns within two seconds where possible and preserve a reliable emergency/human handoff path.
Scale to 100k concurrent conversations and bursty campaign traffic without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Omnichannel contact center commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Omnichannel contact center writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Omnichannel contact center version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Omnichannel contact center by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Omnichannel contact center work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Omnichannel contact center projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Omnichannel contact center projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Omnichannel contact center records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Omnichannel contact center latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
